target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ (D Ic Rc E : Type) (u1 : D → Ic) (u2 : D → Rc) (c2 : Ic → Set E) (c4 : Rc → E)
    (Y V2 : Set D),
    Y ⊆ V2 ∧ (∃ f : Rc → Ic, ∀ o ∈ V2, u1 o = f (u2 o)) ∧
    (¬ ∃ o ∈ Y, c4 (u2 o) ∉ c2 (u1 o)) ∧ (∃ o ∈ V2, c4 (u2 o) ∉ c2 (u1 o))
a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. There exist types D, Ic, Rc, E, then functions u1 from D to Ic, u2 from D to Rc, c2 from Ic to sets of elements of E, and c4 from Rc to E, then subsets Y and V2 of D, such that all four conditions hold: (1) Y is a subset of V2. (2) There exists a single function f from Rc to Ic such that for every o in V2, u1(o) = f(u2(o)). The function is defined on all of Rc, but the equality is required only for o in V2. (3) There is no o in Y for which c4(u2(o)) is outside c2(u1(o)); equivalently, every o in Y satisfies the membership condition. (4) There exists at least one o in V2 for which c4(u2(o)) is outside c2(u1(o)). Such a witness must lie outside Y, so Y is a proper subset of V2, although Y need not be nonempty."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. There exist types D, Ic, Rc, E, then functions u1 from D to Ic, u2 from D to Rc, c2 from Ic to sets of elements of E, and c4 from Rc to E, then subsets Y and V2 of D, such that all four conditions hold: (1) Y is a subset of V2. (2) There exists a single function f from Rc to Ic such that for every o in V2, u1(o) = f(u2(o)). The function is defined on all of Rc, but the equality is required only for o in V2. (3) There is no o in Y for which c4(u2(o)) is outside c2(u1(o)); equivalently, every o in Y satisfies the membership condition. (4) There exists at least one o in V2 for which c4(u2(o)) is outside c2(u1(o)). Such a witness must lie outside Y, so Y is a proper subset of V2, although Y need not be nonempty.

judgement.summary: The target requires strict dependence on V2, no falsification on Y, and a falsification on V2, exactly as claimed. The falsifying dataset must have inference content absent from Y: otherwise strict dependence would give a dataset in Y with the same prediction content and hence the same falsification.
